## What is R Markdown?

R Markdown, like the newer and closely related QuartoMarkdown, is a more flexible alternative to Latex, Word and PowerPoint - or an expansion.

What it can do:

-   Scientific papers, presentations...
-   Books, interactive websites...
-   Apps, videos..

## Necessary installations:

To follow along this workshop, you need to install:

-   [R](https://cran.r-project.org/)

-   [RStudio](https://posit.co/downloads/) (The free version is entirely sufficient)

-   Latex.
    I recommend to install it as a R package:

````{verbatim}
```{r}
install.packages("tinytex")
tinytex::install_tinytex()
```
````

In R Markdown documents, R code is always displayed in grey boxes like this.
The code above first downloads the R package that connects R to Latex, then it downloads Latex itself.

## How to use rticles:

'rticles' is a library with templates for scientific articles.
Install it with the following command:

````{verbatim}
```{r}
install.packages("rticles")
```
````

Then, open a new document.
File -\> New File -\> R Markdown -\> From Template

For this workshop, we will look at the template for American Economics Association journals.
If you selected it and clicked 'OK', a new document will open.

For people who know Latex, this will look familiar - although this is an R Markdown document, it mostly contains Latex code.

## Latex in R Markdown:

An R Markdown document 'understands' most Latex code. It will render a formula like

```{verbatim}
$y_{ij} = x_{ij}\beta_1 + x_{ij}^2\beta_2 + \epsilon$
```

as: $y_{ij} = x_{ij}\beta_1 + x_{ij}^2\beta_2 + \epsilon$.

Each R Markdown document starts with a Yaml header (seperated by `` `---` `` from the rest of the document). Latex packages can be added by inserting the following code into the Yaml header:

```{verbatim}
header-includes: 
 - \usepackage{graphicx}
```
Take care: Yaml is sensitive in regards to indentations.

## Adding a bibliography:

Latex users will already be familiar with bibliography files ending on '.bib'.
They can be added to the Yaml header, too:

```{verbatim}
bibliography: Cherry_blossoms.bib
```

You can cite by naming the key of a paper like `@aonoClarifyingSpringtimeTemperature2010` and it will appear in the text as: @aonoClarifyingSpringtimeTemperature2010.

A bibliography of all sources cited in the text is automatically created at the end of the document.

If you do not have a '.bib'-file yet, you can generate it in all common citation management programmes like Zotero and Citavi.

## Next steps:

Now we know the basics of how to write a paper in R Markdown.
But what truly makes it powerful is that you can run a scientific analysis in the same document that will become your research paper.

It is also easy to set up this analysis in a way that anyone can reproduce it.
In the next step, we will conduct a reproducible research project analyzing the times when cherry blossoms bloom in Japan.
